claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a related fcc high-entropy alloy has high saturation magnetization and coercivity no greater than 100 Oe.
Annealing at approximately 400–600 °C can activate sufficient diffusion to induce limited nanoscale precipitation in FeCoNi or a closely related fcc derivative.
The proposed annealing can produce nanoscale ordered or chemically distinct precipitates embedded in an fcc matrix.
The precipitation treatment can be conducted without significant grain growth or complete phase transformation.
Nanoscale precipitates act as magnetic domain-wall pinning sites.
The precipitates may introduce local variations in magnetic anisotropy.
Precipitate-induced pinning and anisotropy variations inhibit domain-wall motion during magnetization reversal.
Annealing-induced phase separation should increase coercivity relative to the initial single-phase material.
The treatment should raise coercivity to well above 100 Oe.
The treatment should largely retain the high saturation magnetization of the fcc phase.
Keeping the composition close to FeCoNi will preserve high saturation magnetization.
Excessive grain growth or complete phase transformation would compromise the desired magnetic properties.
The coercivity enhancement depends on precipitate size, volume fraction, interfacial coherency, and spatial distribution.

contradictions.description: The falsification rule treats coercivity at or below about 100 Oe as equivalent to no statistically significant enhancement. If the untreated baseline is substantially below 100 Oe, an annealed value below 100 Oe could still be a statistically significant increase, so the threshold and relative-change criteria are not equivalent.
